All controls are referenced from an addon-owned UI file with @uc.<name>.

Element Variables What it does uc.function_panel None Reads #item_id_aux from container_items and is visible while the bound numeric item ID is below 1. Used for an empty/absent-state overlay. uc.second_function_panel None Inverse of function_panel; visible when the numeric item ID is 1 or greater. uc.hover_text_function_panel $function_item_name required Visible when #hover_text does not contain the supplied function marker. uc.second_hover_text_function_panel $function_item_name required Inverse hover-text condition; visible when the marker is present. These are binding templates. Set collection_index on the inherited instance so the collection binding reads the intended helper-entity slot. { "empty_overlay@uc.function_panel": { "collection_index": 3, "controls": [ { "ghost": { "type": "image", "texture": "textures/items/example_input_ghost", "alpha": 0.5 } } ] } }

Draws a purple tooltip-style image with a localized label. Variable Type Default Purpose $hover_text string "" Text or localization key shown in the tooltip. The control is anchored at the top-left, offset [23, 2], placed at layer 80, and does not clip its content.

An invisible 16×16 button whose hover state creates uc.fake_hover_text. Variable Type Default $hover_text string "" Use it when a normal JSON UI control needs a tooltip but is not itself a container slot.

Element Variables Purpose uc.slot_button_prototype None Extends common.container_slot_button_prototype and maps mouse, controller, auto-place, and inventory-drop inputs to button.container_auto_place. uc.slot_button $highlight_control = "uc.slot_highlight" Button wrapper that displays the selected highlight control on hover. uc.slot_highlight None Uses common.hover_text bound to the current item collection's #hover_text. Change $highlight_control only when providing a compatible control reference with the same hover responsibilities.

Reads text from the instance's collection_index, anchors it top-left, and renders it with the current label compatibility logic. Variable Type Default Purpose $text_scale number 1 font_scale_factor for both internal label variants. { "description@uc.text_label": { "collection_index": 1, "anchor_from": "top_left", "anchor_to": "top_left", "offset": [14, 12], "size": [48, 48], "$text_scale": 0.55 } }
Same data source and $text_scale, but uses a 52×52 panel with a centered 48-pixel-wide text area.

Internal label implementations used by both wrappers. Element Bound text Behavior _text_label_v1 #hover_text Direct collection binding. _text_label_v2 #displaying_text Visibility-change binding that remains visible only while the always-bound and displayed text agree or the always-bound text is empty. Both accept $text_scale with default 1. Prefer text_label or centered_text_label rather than referencing these primitives directly.

Wraps chest.chest_label, which displays the current container title. Variable Type Default Purpose $offset [number, number] [10, 0] Title offset inside the machine panel. { "machine_name@uc.machine_name": {} } The visible text comes from the helper entity/container title and its language entry; it is not passed as a UI variable.

A collection_panel that sends button.drop_all when pressed. DoriosCore/DoriosLib interface logic interprets the helper item and button action. Variable Type Default $item_collection_name string "container_items" $button_size [number, number] [18, 18] $button_text string " " $text_scale number 1 $default_texture texture path textures/ui/buttons/power_button $hover_texture texture path textures/ui/buttons/power_button_selected $pressed_texture texture path textures/ui/buttons/power_button_pressed

Uses the same collection, size, scale, texture variables, mappings, and click sound. Instead of $button_text, its label is bound to the selected collection item's #hover_text. { "increase@uc.machine_button": { "collection_index": 4, "$button_size": [24, 16], "$button_text": "+1", "$text_scale": 0.6, "$default_texture": "textures/ui/buttons/button", "$hover_texture": "textures/ui/buttons/button_selected", "$pressed_texture": "textures/ui/buttons/button_pressed" } } default hover pressed
An empty collection_panel template sized to its children. It accepts $item_collection_name, defaulting to container_items, and is useful as a collection-bound base for addon-owned slot compositions.

These controls render items already present in the machine helper entity's container_items collection. They do not create an inventory, move items, or choose an IO mode. The script and entity definition own that behavior; JSON UI only displays the corresponding collection index.

Element Cell / renderer size Hover Intended use uc.button_item_display 18 / 16 Button behavior Small collection-backed button icon. uc.item_display 18 / 16 No Small read-only item or state frame. uc.item_display_medium 34 / 32 No Medium read-only item. uc.item_display_large 50 / 48 No Large read-only resource fill or illustration. uc.item_display_hover 18 / 16 Yes Small item with item tooltip and focus navigation. uc.item_display_hover_medium 34 / 32 Yes Medium item with tooltip. uc.item_display_hover_large 50 / 48 Yes Large item with tooltip; used by resource bars. uc.progress_display 34 / 32 No Animated progress-frame item. Focus navigation is disabled. uc.output_item 26 / 26 Native slot Large output item primitive. uc.input_item 18 / 18 Native slot Standard container item primitive. Display a script-updated progress frame { "progress@uc.progress_display": { "collection_index": 2, "offset": [28, 23] } } progress_display does not calculate progress. The machine script updates the item at index 2 to the correct frame identifier, and the UI renders that item.

The display controls expose the variables below. A wrapper may fix some values to its documented size. Variable Type Default Purpose $cell_image_size [number, number] Depends on control Overall cell image size. $cell_overlay_ref control reference "common.cell_overlay" Overlay used for stack count, durability, and storage indicators. $stack_count_required boolean true Enables the stack-count overlay. $durability_bar_required boolean true Enables the durability overlay when applicable. $storage_bar_required boolean true Enables the storage overlay when applicable. $item_renderer control reference "common.item_renderer" Minecraft item-renderer control. $item_renderer_panel_size [number, number] Depends on control Panel containing the rendered item. $item_renderer_size [number, number] Depends on control Rendered item size. $item_renderer_offset [number, number] [0, 0] Item offset inside its renderer panel. Hover variants additionally accept: Variable Type Default Purpose $button_ref control reference "uc.slot_button" Button/tooltip implementation placed over the item. $focus_id string "" Controller focus identifier. $focus_override_up string "" Explicit focus destination when moving up. $focus_override_down string "" Explicit focus destination when moving down. $focus_override_left string "" Explicit focus destination when moving left. $focus_override_right string "" Explicit focus destination when moving right.

uc._slot_visual and uc._slot_visual_hover implement the renderer, overlay, count, durability/storage bars, and focus bindings used by the public controls. _slot_visual_hover also accepts $button_ref. Their remaining variables are the common item-renderer and focus variables listed above. Prefer a public item_display* wrapper unless you are building a new shared UI abstraction and need full control over the renderer internals.

Element Size Variables What it displays uc.input_slot 18x18 $slot_background_texture = textures/ui/slots/input_1_slot Interactive container item with an input outline. uc.fuel_slot 18x18 None Interactive container item with the fuel outline. uc.upgrade_slot 18x18 $show_slot_background = true Interactive upgrade slot; its outline can be hidden. uc.output_slot 26x26 $slot_background_texture = textures/ui/slots/output_1_slot Larger interactive container item with an output outline. Input, progress, and output { "input@uc.input_slot": { "collection_index": 3, "offset": [0, 30] } }, { "progress@uc.progress_display": { "collection_index": 2, "offset": [28, 23] } }, { "output@uc.output_slot": { "collection_index": 4, "offset": [56, 26] } } Slot names are exact The recognized numbered controls are input_1_slot through input_9_slot and output_1_slot through output_9_slot. Names such as input_1, input_2, or output_1 are not UI Core controls.

uc.input_1_slot through uc.input_9_slot inherit uc.input_slot and set the matching outline texture. Use the number assigned by the machine's IO definition. { "secondary_input@uc.input_2_slot": { "collection_index": 4, "offset": [18, 30] } } input_1_slot input_2_slot input_3_slot input_4_slot input_5_slot input_6_slot input_7_slot input_8_slot input_9_slot

uc.output_1_slot through uc.output_9_slot inherit uc.output_slot and select the matching output outline. output_1_slot output_2_slot output_3_slot output_4_slot output_5_slot output_6_slot output_7_slot output_8_slot output_9_slot

These textures are also consumed by uc.io_face_outline to explain the state encoded by an IO button item. default disabled / none normal both upgrade fuel item resource liquid resource gas resource energy

The standard right-side machine tabs share one radio-toggle group. Opening upgrades, IO, or information selects that tab; selecting the close state hides the active panel. Keep the default shared group names unless you intentionally build more than one independent tab set in the same screen. upgrades closed upgrades open IO closed IO open info closed info open

{ "upgrades@uc.upgrades_tab": { "$upgrade_index_1": 5, "$upgrade_index_2": 6, "$has_first_upgrade": true, "$has_second_upgrade": true } }, { "io@uc.io_tab": { "$has_item_io": true, "$has_fluid_io": true, "$has_gas_io": false, "$io_item_top_index": 8, "$io_fluid_top_index": 14 } }, { "info@uc.info_tab": { "$info_description": "ui.example:info.machine" } } All three controls default $item_collection_name to container_items. upgrades_tab, io_tab, and info_tab also default $right_machine_tabs_name to right_machine_tabs, which makes them mutually exclusive.

Creates the standard upgrades button and panel. The panel supports up to four upgrade slots. Variable Type Default Purpose $item_collection_name string "container_items" Collection containing upgrade items. $upgrade_index_1 ... $upgrade_index_4 number 4, 5, 6, 7 Collection index for each upgrade slot. $has_first_upgrade boolean true Shows slot 1. $has_second_upgrade boolean true Shows slot 2. $has_third_upgrade boolean false Shows slot 3. $has_fourth_upgrade boolean false Shows slot 4. $upgrade_overlay_1 texture path textures/items/machinery/speed_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 1. $upgrade_overlay_2 texture path textures/items/machinery/energy_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 2. $upgrade_overlay_3 texture path textures/items/machinery/range_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 3. $upgrade_overlay_4 texture path textures/items/machinery/quantity_upgrade Empty-slot guide for slot 4. $right_machine_tabs_name string "right_machine_tabs" Shared radio-toggle group. $upgrade_toggle_control_name string "upgrade_toggle_button" Binding name used to open and close the panel. The UI overlays are visual hints only. The machine's registered upgrade slots and upgrade definitions determine which items are accepted and which values are modified.

Creates the standard IO button and configuration panel. It can expose separate item, liquid, and gas pages. Each page contains six block-face buttons in this order: top, left, front, right, bottom, back.

Variable Type Default Purpose $item_collection_name string "container_items" Collection containing IO button items. $info_description string "" Reserved description value passed by the shared panel. $has_io_config boolean true Shows the IO configuration feature. $has_item_io boolean true Shows the item page selector and face controls. $has_fluid_io boolean false Shows the liquid page selector and face controls. $has_gas_io boolean false Shows the gas page selector and face controls. $io_items_default boolean true Initial checked state for the item selector. $io_fluids_default boolean false Initial checked state for the liquid selector. $io_gases_default boolean false Initial checked state for the gas selector. $io_default_tab_index number 0 Forced selected index in the item/liquid/gas radio group. $right_machine_tabs_name string "right_machine_tabs" Shared right-side tab group. $io_toggle_control_name string "io_toggle_button" Open/close binding name. $io_config_tabs_name string "io_config_tabs" Item/liquid/gas radio group name. $io_items_toggle_control_name string "io_items_toggle_button" Item-page binding name. $io_fluids_toggle_control_name string "io_fluids_toggle_button" Liquid-page binding name. $io_gases_toggle_control_name string "io_gases_toggle_button" Gas-page binding name. The three default mode descriptions are IO Modes: followed by blue inputs 1-9 and red outputs 1-9. Override them when a machine supports fewer modes or additional semantic roles: { "io@uc.io_tab": { "$has_item_io": true, "$has_fluid_io": true, "$io_items_modes_description": "§rItem IO Modes:
§r- §9Input 1
§r- §cOutput 1", "$io_fluids_modes_description": "§rLiquid IO Modes:
§r- §9Input 1" } } Use §r at the beginning of every custom formatted line so formatting inherited from another label or item name cannot leak into it.

Resource Top Left Front Right Bottom Back Item $io_item_top_index = 8 $io_item_left_index = 9 $io_item_front_index = 10 $io_item_right_index = 11 $io_item_bottom_index = 12 $io_item_back_index = 13 Liquid $io_fluid_top_index = 14 $io_fluid_left_index = 15 $io_fluid_front_index = 16 $io_fluid_right_index = 17 $io_fluid_bottom_index = 18 $io_fluid_back_index = 19 Gas $io_gas_top_index = 20 $io_gas_left_index = 21 $io_gas_front_index = 22 $io_gas_right_index = 23 $io_gas_bottom_index = 24 $io_gas_back_index = 25 Every visible resource page needs six valid helper-entity indices. The item at each index carries the current IO state in its hover text; clicking the face button dispatches the shared machine-button action.

Variable Default texture $io_top_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_up $io_left_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_west $io_front_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_north $io_right_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_east $io_bottom_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_down $io_back_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_south These six textures visualize block orientation. Override them only when the machine needs a different face diagram. items unchecked items checked liquids unchecked liquids checked gases unchecked gases checked
Normal machines should use uc.io_tab. The following controls are its compositional parts.

Builds the six-face diagram. It accepts $io_top_index, $io_left_index, $io_front_index, $io_right_index, $io_bottom_index, and $io_back_index (defaults 8-13), plus the six $io_*_texture variables listed above.

Combines one machine button, one face texture, and one state outline. Variable Default $item_collection_name "container_items" $io_button_index 0 $io_button_offset [0, 0] $io_face_offset [0, 1] $io_face_texture textures/blocks/machines/exhibitor_base_north

Reads the selected IO button item's hover text and draws the outline matching its exact state marker. Variable family Defaults / accepted states $item_collection_name, $io_button_index, $io_button_offset container_items, 0, [0,0] $io_default_texture, $io_disabled_texture, $io_none_texture, $io_normal_texture Corresponding default, none, and normal slot textures. $io_input_1_texture ... $io_input_9_texture textures/ui/slots/input_1_slot ... input_9_slot. $io_output_1_texture ... $io_output_9_texture textures/ui/slots/output_1_slot ... output_9_slot. $io_both_texture, $io_upgrade_texture, $io_fuel_texture Corresponding slot textures. $io_item_resource_texture, $io_liquid_resource_texture, $io_gas_resource_texture, $io_energy_texture Corresponding resource slot textures. The exact recognized state markers are default, disabled, none, normal, input_1 through input_9, output_1 through output_9, both, upgrade, fuel, item_resource, liquid_resource, gas_resource, and energy. uc.io_state_outline is the internal 18x18 image primitive used once per possible state. It expects $item_collection_name, $io_button_index, $io_button_offset, $io_state_name, and $io_outline_texture from its parent.

Creates a localized, scrollable information panel. Variable Type Default Purpose $item_collection_name string "container_items" Shared collection context. $info_description string "" when omitted Localization key or literal description shown in the scroll area. $right_machine_tabs_name string "right_machine_tabs" Shared right-tab radio group. $info_toggle_control_name string "info_toggle_button" Open/close binding name. uc.info_description_scroll_content is the internal vertical scrolling content. It accepts $info_description, default "". For a normal machine, pass the value to info_tab and let it compose the scroll control.

A reusable Minecraft JSON UI toggle with optional radio grouping, tooltip, background, and icon. Variable group Variables and defaults Identity/state $toggle_name="toggle_button", $toggle_index=0, $toggle_group=false, $toggle_default_state=false, $toggle_group_default_selected=0, $toggle_control_name="" Layout $toggle_layer=0, $toggle_size=[18,18], $toggle_lost_reset=true Tooltip $toggle_hover_text="", $toggle_checked_hover_text="", both localization flags false, $toggle_checked_hover_text_from_hover=false State textures $toggle_unchecked, $toggle_checked, $toggle_unchecked_hover, $toggle_checked_hover use the matching textures/ui/buttons/* defaults Background $has_toggle_bg=false, $toggle_bg_texture="textures/ui/toggle_button/right_bg", $toggle_bg_size=[24,24], $toggle_bg_offset=[0,0], $toggle_bg_layer=-6 Optional icon $has_toggle_icon=false, $toggle_icon_size=[16,16], four $toggle_icon_* texture paths default to "", $toggle_icon_uv_size=[16,16] uc.button_display renders the collection item used as a 16x16 button visual. It accepts $item_collection_name and $collection_index (default 0). uc.toggle_button_panel shows an arbitrary $controls array while the toggle named by $panel_control_name is checked. Both variables default to an empty value.

Estudio Bedrock independiente · Desde 2022 Equipo pequeño. Mundos más grandes. Dorios Studios es un colectivo de creadores que desarrolla addons gratuitos para Minecraft Bedrock con sistemas útiles, progreso deliberado y una comunidad que sigue dando forma al trabajo. Conoce al equipo Explora los proyectos Fundación 09.09.2022 Plataforma Minecraft Bedrock Enfoque Addons gratuitos pensados para jugadores Por qué existimos Crear más posibilidades en cada mundo. Creemos que los jugadores de Bedrock deben tener acceso a experiencias ambiciosas y de alta calidad sin poner las ideas más interesantes detrás de un pago. Nuestro trabajo abarca desde automatización industrial hasta exploración y mecánicas personalizadas, siempre con el mismo estándar: accesible al inicio, gratificante como sistema y digno de compartir. Nuestra historia Construida mediante iteración. De experimentos individuales a un colectivo multidisciplinario de Bedrock. 2020 Los primeros experimentos Milo504 comenzó a crear addons de Bedrock con More Armors, seguido de Tools, Weapons and More, el proyecto que con el tiempo se convertiría en UtilityCraft. 2022 Dorios Studios toma forma Milo504 y WeatherVictor fundaron Dorios Studios el 9 de septiembre, uniendo desarrollo y diseño de interfaces bajo una identidad compartida. 2024 Un lenguaje visual más claro JR.ice se unió como diseñador principal y artista de texturas. Después llegó UtilityCraft 3.0, el primer gran hito del estudio en la comunidad Bedrock. Nuestro enfoque Principios que sobreviven al prototipo. Abre un principio para ver cómo guía el trabajo. 01Bedrock primeroDiseñar para la plataforma que los jugadores realmente usan.+ Los controles, el multijugador, el rendimiento y el ecosistema de addons Bedrock guían cada decisión desde el principio; no son una adaptación al final. 02Sistemas con propósitoDar a cada mecánica un lugar en el progreso.+ La automatización útil, un progreso claro y el espacio para experimentar convierten funciones aisladas en mundos que siguen siendo interesantes mañana. 03Moldeado por la comunidadTratar los comentarios como parte del trabajo.+ Los jugadores y probadores ayudan a revelar qué es confuso, está desequilibrado o todavía no es divertido. Sus comentarios orientan la evolución de los addons. Dentro del estudio Personas y agradecimientos. El equipo registra quién hace el trabajo. Los créditos registran a todas las personas y herramientas que lo hacen posible. 01 / Personas Equipo Conoce al equipo del estudio, sus disciplinas principales y los creadores que colaboran con nosotros. Ver equipo 02 / Agradecimientos Créditos Colaboradores, probadores, apoyo de la comunidad y herramientas de código abierto detrás del sitio. Leer créditos Comunidad y valores Los comentarios son parte del proceso. Comparte lo que funciona, reporta lo que no y ayúdanos a entender qué quieren construir después los jugadores de Bedrock. Los comentarios cuidadosos fortalecen cada lanzamiento. Únete a la conversación Apoya al estudio

ProyectosAscendant TechnologyAscendant Technology Wiki Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl K Bloques Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl KExplorar Ascendant Technology Resumen Resumen Contenido ObjetosBloques Sistemas MáquinasGeneradores Referencia RecetasMecánicas Repositorio de GitHub ← Volver a Bloques Bloque registro Universal Exporter Extrae recursos del inventario o tanque de origen conectado y los envía a destinos compatibles de la red. BloqueOverworldMaquinaria ResumenEspecificacionesRecetas Identificador utilitycraft:universal_exporter Block type Bloque Nivel Maquinaria Break time 1 s Funcionamiento del transporte Extrae recursos del inventario o tanque de origen conectado y los envía a destinos compatibles de la red. Dirección Origen → red → destino Filtro Instala una Mejora de Filtro: la lista de permitidos acepta los recursos indicados; la lista de bloqueados los excluye. Filtro de objetos vacío Con el filtro instalado, una lista de permitidos vacía bloquea la exportación; una lista de bloqueados vacía permite todos los objetos. Modos de distribución Nearest prioriza los destinos más cercanos; Farthest prioriza los más lejanos; Round Robin alterna el siguiente destino tras una transferencia exitosa. Caudal estimado de objetos Exporter: una operación cada 10 ticks, hasta 64 objetos por operación; aproximadamente 128 objetos/s con pilas completas. Cuatro Mejoras de Velocidad elevan el límite a cinco operaciones/ciclo, hasta 640 objetos/s. Caudal de líquidos y gases Límite del Exporter: 4.000 mB por ciclo, multiplicado por 1–5 con Mejoras de Velocidad. Cada recurso utiliza su propio límite de transferencia. Configuración de recursos Los objetos, líquidos y gases se configuran por separado en el menú del terminal. Conexión de energía También conecta la red de energía por sus caras habilitadas. Los ajustes de objetos, líquidos y gases pertenecen a sus respectivos sistemas de transferencia. Conexiones Los colores de tubos compatibles y las caras habilitadas deben conectar el origen con los destinos. Configura las caras con la Llave Inglesa; copia ajustes compatibles con la herramienta de copiar y pegar. Las estimaciones nominales suponen 20 ticks de juego/s. El tamaño de las pilas, los filtros, los objetos disponibles, el espacio libre, las caras de entrada y salida y los chunks cargados pueden reducir el caudal real.

Dorios Energy The shared power network used by Ascendant machines, storage, relays, Power Beacons, and absolute-tier infrastructure. Gas Management The gas input, storage, processing, and output system used by supported superior machines and recipes. Superior Machines Advanced processors with specialized item, liquid, gas, catalyst, and upgrade slots for late-game production. Absolute Generators The fifth generator tier, built to supply high-output Dorios Energy for Ascendant industrial networks. Cryogenic Branches Cryogenic work is split between the Cryo Freezer, Cryofluid Synthesizer, and Cryo Stabilizer so each production lane can scale independently. Overclock Network An Overclock Tower consumes fuel, Reinforced Cable carries the network, and Overclock Relays distribute the selected boost to supported machines. Progression Status Aetherium, Titanium, and Tungsten are documented current materials. Niobium, Singularities, and Kyarium remain planned progression; the Singularity Fabricator is pending rework. End-game architecture Specialized machines, shared industrial core. Ascendant Technology raises infrastructure costs and process complexity while keeping energy, fluids, recipes, and machine state compatible with UtilityCraft.

Velocidad estimada Cada 10 ticks: una operación de pila, ampliada a nueve con ocho Mejoras de Velocidad. A 20 ticks/s: unas 2–18 operaciones de pila/s, según los objetos y la capacidad disponibles. Distribución Requiere una red de almacenamiento vinculada y activa. Utiliza el orden de las ranuras para distribuir los objetos. Las estimaciones nominales suponen 20 ticks de juego/s. Dorios Energy The UtilityCraft power system used by multiblock controllers, energy ports, storage components, factories, and generators. Fluid Management The liquid input, storage, transfer, and output system used by chambers, reactors, tanks, and multiblock ports. Multiblock Machines Expandable processing factories assembled from one controller, compatible casings, ports, and internal modules. Multiblock Generators Large structures that generate, buffer, and distribute Dorios Energy through configurable internal components. Uranium Fuel Cycle Raw uranium is processed into uranium products, converted into uranium hexafluoride, enriched in the Isotope Centrifuge, formed into Enriched Uranium Fuel Rods, and consumed by the Nuclear Reactor while producing waste gas. Hazard Equipment Hazmat pieces carry the shared hazard-equipment tag and offer repairable armor protection. Utility Exo pieces provide extremely durable wearable equipment; special abilities are documented only when implemented. Modular Storage Liquid and Gas Tank Controllers form steel-cased storage structures with five independent channels. Cells add capacity and compatible ports provide per-face automation. Construction rule One controller. One valid shell. Your choice of internals. The controller indexes every compatible component inside the detected structure. This makes size and module distribution part of the machine design rather than a fixed recipe.

Filtro Una Mejora de Filtro habilita una lista de permitidos o bloqueados por tipo de objeto. El filtro se aplica a la recogida y a la salida. Velocidad estimada Un ciclo cada 8 ticks (unos 2,5 ciclos/s). Cada paso de recogida/salida intenta mover 1–5 pilas con 0–4 Mejoras de Velocidad: unos 2,5–12,5 intentos de pila/s por paso. Distribución Utiliza su dirección física de salida. Nearest, Farthest y Round Robin son modos de los Exporters de red. Radio de recogida Predeterminado: 3 bloques; cada Mejora de Alcance añade 2 bloques, hasta 11. El radio se puede reducir en el menú. Las estimaciones nominales suponen 20 ticks de juego/s. El tamaño de las pilas, los filtros, los objetos disponibles, el espacio libre, las caras de entrada y salida y los chunks cargados pueden reducir el caudal real.

ProyectosUtilityCraftUtilityCraft Wiki Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl K Bloques Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl KExplorar UtilityCraft Resumen Resumen Cómo jugar Contenido ObjetosBloques Sistemas MáquinasGeneradores Referencia RecetasMecánicas Repositorio de GitHub ← Volver a Bloques Bloque registro Exportador de Objetos Extrae recursos del inventario o tanque de origen conectado y los envía a destinos compatibles de la red. BloqueOverworldMaquinaria ResumenEspecificacionesRecetas Identificador utilitycraft:item_exporter Block type Bloque Nivel Maquinaria Break time 1 s Funcionamiento del transporte Extrae recursos del inventario o tanque de origen conectado y los envía a destinos compatibles de la red. Dirección Origen → red → destino Filtro Instala una Mejora de Filtro: la lista de permitidos acepta los recursos indicados; la lista de bloqueados los excluye. Filtro de objetos vacío Con el filtro instalado, una lista de permitidos vacía bloquea la exportación; una lista de bloqueados vacía permite todos los objetos. Modos de distribución Nearest prioriza los destinos más cercanos; Farthest prioriza los más lejanos; Round Robin alterna el siguiente destino tras una transferencia exitosa. Caudal estimado de objetos Exporter: una operación cada 10 ticks, hasta 64 objetos por operación; aproximadamente 128 objetos/s con pilas completas. Cuatro Mejoras de Velocidad elevan el límite a cinco operaciones/ciclo, hasta 640 objetos/s. Conexiones Los colores de tubos compatibles y las caras habilitadas deben conectar el origen con los destinos. Configura las caras con la Llave Inglesa; copia ajustes compatibles con la herramienta de copiar y pegar. Las estimaciones nominales suponen 20 ticks de juego/s. El tamaño de las pilas, los filtros, los objetos disponibles, el espacio libre, las caras de entrada y salida y los chunks cargados pueden reducir el caudal real.

UtilityCraft reshapes survival from the first day onward: start with simple tools and renewable resources, then grow into powered machines, storage, transport, and full automation. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 Resources, tools and utility Begin with hammers, pebbles, sieves, and mesh progression. Those early loops become a reliable source of ores, seeds, and building materials. Crops, tools, cobblestone generators, and utility blocks reduce repetitive work while keeping the survival progression intact. 02 Machines and energy Machines, generators, batteries, and upgrades form the heart of UtilityCraft automation. Process items, route Dorios Energy, and scale a small workshop into a factory. Liquid tanks and mob-grinding systems extend the same production network with fluid storage, automated drops, and experience handling. 03 Your progression path 01 Gather pebbles and loose materials with a Wooden or Stone Hammer. 02 Craft a Flint Knife, String Mesh, and Sieve to unlock renewable resources. 03 Scale sieving, produce Water and Lava, then prepare Steel. 04 Craft the UtilityCraft Workbench and enter the Machinery Era. 05 Generate Dorios Energy, power machines, and automate your production lines. Increase throughput before automation by expanding the Sieve setup and choosing the right efficiency tradeoff. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 Scale up Sieving Place Sieves next to one another to grow from a single Sieve into a 3×3 and finally a 5×5 array. Up to 25 Sieves can work together. A larger array processes stacks of Gravel, Dirt, or Sand much faster. Collect extra Gravel early so you can craft the next Flint Mesh tier. 02 Upgrade Meshes Higher-tier Meshes improve eligible drops and output multipliers. Upgrade as the world expands so rare resources do not become a bottleneck. 01 Hilo 02 Flint 03 Cobre 04 Hierro 05 Gold 06 Esmeralda 07 Diamante 08 Netherite 03 Process compressed resources Compress Cobblestone, Gravel, Dirt, or Sand for bulk handling. Hammers reduce compressed blocks through the same material sequence. The Sieve accepts compressed blocks and processes them faster, but the in-game guide notes an output of roughly 50% compared with normal blocks. Use this when speed matters more than efficiency. Turn renewable early resources into Steel, unlock the Workbench, and prepare the materials needed for powered production. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 Produce acero con la Forja Primitiva Sigue el tutorial de la Forja Primitiva para combinar polvo de hierro con carbono y después fundir el acero en bruto en lingotes de acero. El método con SmeltFlare de abajo es otra forma de obtener acero. Construye una Forja Primitiva y produce acero.→ 02 1. Craft the SmeltFlare The SmeltFlare combines raw materials directly in your inventory. Obtain Paper by sieving Dirt for Sugar Cane, then craft the Sugar Cane into Paper. 03 2. Create Brute Steel Keep a SmeltFlare, Raw Iron, and Coal together in your inventory to form Brute Steel. Smelt Brute Steel in a Furnace or use another SmeltFlare to produce Steel Ingots. You can combine nine Brute Steel into a block and smelt the full batch at once. 04 3. Craft the Workbench Every UtilityCraft Machine, Generator, and machine Upgrade is crafted inside the Workbench. Keep Steel, Iron, Copper, Redstone, and Coal stocked for the next stage. 05 4. Power your first system 01 Craft an early generator, such as the Basic Furnator. 02 Connect or place a powered Machine in the Dorios Energy network. 03 Buffer excess power in a Battery. 04 Add Speed or Energy upgrades only after generation is stable. Every generator family has four progression tiers. Choose fuel and placement around the production line you want to sustain. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 Generator families Furnator Burns solid fuel into Energy and is the simplest early generator. Nivel 1 40 DE/t Nivel 2 160 DE/t Nivel 3 640 DE/t Nivel 4 4000 DE/t Magmator Turns Lava into Energy and pairs naturally with Crucibles and fluid transport. Nivel 1 50 DE/t Nivel 2 200 DE/t Nivel 3 800 DE/t Nivel 4 5000 DE/t Solar Panel Produces passive, fuel-free Energy when it has clear access to sunlight. Nivel 1 12 DE/t Nivel 2 48 DE/t Nivel 3 192 DE/t Nivel 4 1200 DE/t Thermo Generator Produces steady Energy from heat sources without consuming item fuel. Nivel 1 20 DE/t Nivel 2 80 DE/t Nivel 3 320 DE/t Nivel 4 2000 DE/t Wind Turbine Generates passive Energy in open areas where placement conditions are met. Nivel 1 8 DE/t Nivel 2 32 DE/t Nivel 3 128 DE/t Nivel 4 800 DE/t 02 Store excess Energy Batteries keep machines working when generation slows. Their Tier 1–4 capacities are 256k, 1.024M, 4.096M, and 25.6M DE. Anterior← MáquinasPaso siguienteDrop Tables →

ProyectosUtilityCraftUtilityCraft Wiki Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl K Getting Started Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl KExplorar UtilityCraft Resumen Resumen Cómo jugar IntroductionGetting StartedExpanding ResourcesWater & LavaPrimitive ForgeFirst Steps to SteelMachinesGeneratorsDrop Tables Contenido ObjetosBloques Sistemas MáquinasGeneradores Referencia RecetasMecánicas Repositorio de GitHub Stage 01 · Early survival Paso 02 de 09 Tools, pebbles, and your first Sieve. Secure the basic tools that turn ordinary blocks into a renewable resource loop. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 1. Craft a Hammer Save at least one log from your first tree. Use planks, logs, and sticks to craft a Wooden Hammer; upgrade to Stone when you can. While holding the Hammer, sneak and interact with Dirt or Grass to find pebbles and loose materials. Combine four matching pebbles to rebuild their full block. Special find Cantidad Source block Probabilidad Sand Handful 1 Dirt / Grass 20% Mud Ball 1 Mud 50% Red Sand Handful 1 Red Sand / Terracotta 50% 02 2. Make a Flint Knife Use a Flint Knife to break Leaves and collect Fiber. Craft Fiber into String for your first Mesh. If Flint is scarce, combine three Gravel to craft one. Without String, the Sieve cannot be used. 03 3. Build the Sieve loop Craft a Sieve and a String Mesh, place the mesh inside, then process Gravel, Dirt, or Sand. Better meshes later unlock stronger drops and multipliers. Use the Hammer to reduce blocks in order: Cobblestone → Gravel → Dirt → Sand. Combine hammering with sieving for a fully renewable early-game loop. 01 Break Cobblestone into Gravel. 02 Sieve Gravel for ore chunks, Lapis, and gem shards. 03 Break Gravel into Dirt and sieve it for seeds and saplings. 04 Break Dirt into Sand and sieve it for Redstone and other resources. 04 4. Check your foundation Before moving on, keep a Hammer, a Flint Knife, and a Sieve fitted with a String Mesh. You should now have renewable String, Gravel, Dirt, Sand, ores, and seeds. Most UtilityCraft machines consume Dorios Energy, can output toward a configured side, and accept upgrades for speed or efficiency. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 Machine directory Assembler Repeats a crafting pattern stored on a Blueprint made by the Digitizer. Accepts Speed and Energy upgrades. Tamizadora Automática Processes sieveable blocks with a Mesh. Better Meshes unlock stronger drops and multipliers. Autofisher Generates fishing loot with Fishing Nets. Better Nets improve rolls, luck, and rare drops. Block Breaker Uses an installed Pickaxe to break the block directly in front of it. Block Placer Places inventory blocks into the space ahead; pair it with a Block Breaker for loops. Triturador Turns ores into dust and applies specialized yields to mineral resources. Digitizer Records crafting layouts on Blueprint Paper for use in an Assembler. Prensa Eléctrica Automates plates, compression, ore reconstruction, and complete-gem assembly. Harvester Harvests mature crops and resets growth. Range upgrades expand the work area. Incinerador Smelts valid inputs with Dorios Energy instead of furnace fuel. Induction Anvil Repairs tools, armor, and other durable items using Energy. Infusor Combines an input with a catalyst to create infused materials and components. Magmatic Chamber Handles heat and lava processing with both item and liquid support. Seed Synthesizer Creates special seeds through high-energy powered synthesis. ProyectosUtilityCraftUtilityCraft Wiki Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl K Primitive Forge Buscar en esta sección de la wikiCtrl KExplorar UtilityCraft Resumen Resumen Cómo jugar IntroductionGetting StartedExpanding ResourcesWater & LavaPrimitive ForgeFirst Steps to SteelMachinesGeneratorsDrop Tables Contenido ObjetosBloques Sistemas MáquinasGeneradores Referencia RecetasMecánicas Repositorio de GitHub Metalurgia inicial · Combustible sólido Paso 05 de 09 Construye una Forja Primitiva y produce acero. Monta ocho bloques de forja, añade combustible sólido y usa las dos ranuras de ingredientes para fundir materiales o combinar polvo de hierro con carbono. No requiere generador. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 1. Fabrica ocho bloques de forja Usa una mesa de trabajo normal. Cada fabricación produce cuatro bloques de Forja Primitiva; repítela dos veces para completar la estructura. 01 Fila superior: Ladrillo · Bola de arcilla · Ladrillo. 02 Fila central: Bola de arcilla · vacío · Bola de arcilla. 03 Fila inferior: Ladrillo · Losa de ladrillos de barro · Ladrillo. Ingrediente Por fabricación Forja completa Ladrillo 4 8 Bola de arcilla 3 6 Losa de ladrillos de barro 1 2 Abrir la receta de fabricación de la forja→ 02 2. Monta la estructura 2×2×2 01 Coloca cuatro bloques de Forja Primitiva en un cuadrado 2×2. 02 Coloca cuatro bloques más directamente encima para llenar una segunda capa 2×2. No dejes huecos. 03 La estructura se forma automáticamente al colocar el último bloque. Su frente sigue la orientación de ese bloque. Interactúa con el frente para abrir la forja. 03 3. Añade ingredientes y combustible La interfaz tiene dos ranuras de ingredientes, una ranura separada para combustible sólido, una flecha de progreso, un indicador de combustible y cuatro ranuras de salida en una cuadrícula 2×2. Empieza con carbón o carbón vegetal en la ranura de combustible. Los troncos, tablones, palos y otros combustibles sólidos registrados también funcionan. La forja solo quema combustible mientras procesa; el tiempo restante se conserva mientras está inactiva. El carbono en una ranura de ingredientes forma parte de la receta de acero. Añade combustible adicional en la ranura de combustible. 04 4. Funde materiales normales Coloca un ingrediente fundible compatible en cualquiera de las entradas. Con dos entradas compatibles y sin receta combinada, ambas pueden fundir durante el mismo ciclo. Cada entrada procesa una receta por ciclo. Un ciclo normal tarda 40 ticks (2 segundos a 20 ticks/s); una pila en la ranura alimenta los siguientes ciclos. Las cuatro ranuras de salida sirven como almacenamiento y no aumentan las recetas por entrada. Entrada Result Ciclo 1 Polvo de hierro 1 Lingote de hierro 40 ticks · 2 s 1 Acero en bruto 1 Lingote de acero 40 ticks · 2 s 05 5. Produce acero en bruto y después lingotes de acero Antes de preparar la aleación, extrae mineral de hierro o mineral de hierro de pizarra profunda con un martillo compatible para obtener polvo de hierro. Una Trituradora con energía también puede producirlo más adelante. Usa polvo de hierro para la combinación; el hierro en bruto y los lingotes de hierro no lo sustituyen en esta receta de forja. 01 Coloca polvo de hierro en una ranura de ingredientes. 02 Coloca carbón, carbón vegetal, polvo de carbón o polvo de carbón vegetal en la otra. Puedes invertir el orden de los ingredientes. 03 Suministra combustible sólido por separado y deja espacio libre en la salida. La receta combinada tiene prioridad sobre la fundición normal. 04 Tras 160 ticks (8 segundos a 20 ticks/s), recoge un acero en bruto por cada unidad de polvo de hierro y de carbono consumida. 05 Retira el ingrediente de carbono y coloca el acero en bruto en cualquiera de las entradas. Fúndelo durante 40 ticks para obtener un lingote de acero. Ver todas las recetas de la Forja Primitiva→Ver recetas de polvo de hierro→ 06 6. Mantén la forja funcionando Si el procesamiento se detiene, revisa el montaje de los ocho bloques, los ingredientes de la receta, el combustible disponible y el espacio en la salida. Un ciclo en curso se pausa si los resultados no caben. Cambiar la receta o retirar ingredientes reservados para el ciclo actual reinicia el progreso. Romper un bloque de forja desmonta la estructura y suelta los ingredientes, los objetos de combustible y los productos almacenados. Vacíala antes de moverla. Ver especificaciones de la forja→Avanzar a la Era de las Máquinas→ Anterior← Water & LavaPaso siguienteFirst Steps to Steel →

These fluid loops unlock early automation, farming, Nether access, and the path to your first generator. 01Introduction02Getting Started03Expanding Resources04Water & Lava05Forja Primitiva06First Steps to Steel07Máquinas08Generadores09Drop Tables 01 1. Obtain Water 01 Craft a Mortar with three Cobblestone and one Stone Pebble. 02 Combine the Mortar, one Glass Bottle, and two Saplings to make a Water Bottle. The Mortar is not consumed. 03 Use three Water Bottles on a Cauldron, then collect the water with a Bucket. 02 2. Craft the Crucible The Crucible requires four Bricks and four Mud Bricks. Smelt Clay for Bricks; Clay comes from sieving Sand. Use a Water Bottle on placed Dirt to create Mud, combine Mud with Wheat for Packed Mud, then craft four Packed Mud into one Mud Brick. 03 3. Produce Lava Place the Crucible above a heat source and insert four Cobblestone to slowly produce one bucket of Lava. Stronger heat sources finish faster. Heat source Heat value Lava / Flowing Lava 4 Soul Fire / Soul Torch / Soul Campfire 4 Fire / Campfire / Magma Block 3 Torch 1 04 4. Make Obsidian Interact with a Crucible using a Water Bucket to create Obsidian instantly. Stable Water and Lava production now gives you the foundation for energy generation.
